title: Partial Title Added Entries
summary: Partial title added entries (740/246) are no longer made for subject cataloging purposes (practice ended January 1995). Where a significant title term is not covered by subject headings, it may be recorded in a 653 uncontrolled-term field per H 160, without duplicating other searchable fields. Existing partial title added entries are not systematically deleted but are removed during normal maintenance when covered by new headings. Not relevant to validating heading strings.
validation_rules: Do not assign a partial title added entry (740 or 246) for subject cataloging purposes. (H 150 sec. 1)
A significant title term not covered by subject headings may be recorded in a 653 field (per H 160), but not if it duplicates a term in another searchable field. (H 150 sec. 2)

[LC practice] Do not systematically delete old partial title added entries; delete them when covered by newly established headings being added during normal file maintenance (cf. H 200 sec. 14). (H 150 sec. 3)

sections.heading: 1. Partial title added entry not used
sections.text: Do not assign a partial title added entry for subject cataloging purposes, either in a 740 field or a 246 field.

sections.heading: 2. Use of 653 field
sections.text: If there are special circumstances that necessitate recording the varying form of a word appearing in a title that is judged to be significant for subject access but not adequately covered by the assigned subject headings, record the term in a 653 field for uncontrolled subject terms following the procedures in H 160. Do not add a term to the 653 field that duplicates a term appearing in another searchable field.

sections.heading: 3. Deletion of partial title added entries
sections.text: LC practice: Make no systematic attempt to delete partial title added entries assigned for subject cataloging purposes from existing bibliographic records cataloged when the practice was in effect. Delete partial title added entries assigned for subject cataloging purposes when they are covered by newly established subject headings being assigned to existing bibliographic records as part of normal bibliographic file maintenance (cf. H 200, sec. 14).
